# parcelo repo conventions (learned PRC-101, 2026-11-12)
# NOTE: this log is truncated after PRC-143. Results for PRC-144..166 are in ticket-checklist.md and MEMORY.md, so don't append more here.

- Preferred style = parcelo/shipments.py: raise `DomainError(code, msg)` from parcelo/errors.py;
  codes MUST be in `CODES` set there (unregistered code -> RuntimeError). Existing: E_NOT_FOUND,
  E_UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER, E_BAD_ZONE, E_BAD_WEIGHT, E_BAD_STATE, E_BAD_INPUT, E_LIMIT.
- State changes record `audit.record("<entity>.<verb>", id, **details)`; use `clock.now()` and
  `ids.new_id(prefix)` rather than datetime/uuid.
- IDS (review rule, PRC-143): EVERY new entity id comes from `ids.new_id("<3-letter prefix>")` -> `prefix_000001`
  (support tooling parses this format). Never use uuid, f-strings, counters, or hand-built ids anywhere (code OR tests).
  Old modules (invoices.py, customers.py add_customer) still use uuid, so don't copy them, and if you touch a function
  there that creates an id, switch it to ids.new_id. Tests should assert the exact format (`== "pku_000001"` or regex).
  Prefixes used so far: shp, cus?, inv?, ref, adr, clm, pku (read ids.py and existing modules to confirm).
  UPDATE (PRC-140/141): parcelo/events.py may exist (`events.emit(name, entity_id, **payload)` -> `events.OUTBOX`
  list of dicts {name, entity_id, at, payload}; conftest clears it). Modules migrated to it (shipments.py) use emit
  INSTEAD of audit. Before writing a state change, grep the target module for `audit.record` vs `events.emit`
  and use whichever it uses (approved PRC-141). Tests then assert on events.OUTBOX instead of audit.LOG.
- Money: new code uses `parcelo.money.Money` for every currency amount (parse/scale/+ /cents exist).
  Older modules (rates.quote, etc.) return floats, so wrap them with `Money.parse(...)` and return Money.
  There was a past "rounding incident," so reviewers reject floats for money. That includes WRITING a float back into
  a money field (PRC-150 rejected). Store Money unless old float-summing code reads that exact field (PRC-113 only).
- `parcelo/legacy/` is scheduled for deletion. New code/tests must not import it, and you shouldn't modify it.
  Copy any needed logic or constants into the module you're changing.
- invoices.py is OLD style (KeyError/ValueError, print, datetime.utcnow, uuid) — don't copy it.
- Lookup helper `shipments.get_shipment` raises E_NOT_FOUND; reuse it.
- Tests: tests/unit/test_*.py, conftest autouse resets store/ids/audit/clock. `python -m pytest -q`.
  Put each ticket's tests in a NEW file under tests/unit/. See [[ticket-checklist]].
- Shipment statuses seen: "created", "delivered", "cancelled". Repo resets between tickets, so functions
  from earlier tickets (cancel_shipment, mark_delivered...) may be absent. Check before relying on them.

## Ticket log
- PRC-101: added cancel_shipment (E_NOT_FOUND / E_BAD_STATE for cancelled|delivered,
  appends reason to notes, audit "shipment.cancelled") + 4 tests. Suite: 9 passed.
  CI passed, but review REQUESTED CHANGES: (a) no CHANGELOG entry, (b) tests were appended to the
  existing test_shipments.py when they needed a new tests/unit file. Both rules are now in [[ticket-checklist]].
- PRC-102 (2026-11-12): added invoices.void_invoice + Invoice.voided_at. New-style code inside old
  invoices.py (DomainError E_NOT_FOUND / E_BAD_STATE for paid|void, clock.now(), audit "invoice.voided");
  left existing old-style functions untouched. Tests in NEW tests/unit/test_invoices_void.py (4 tests),
  CHANGELOG bullet added. Suite: 9 passed. Note: repo resets between tickets (PRC-101's cancel_shipment
  was absent), so don't assume earlier ticket code exists. Invoice statuses: "open", "paid", "void".
  RESULT: CI passed + review APPROVED on first try. Confirms the full [[ticket-checklist]] works,
  and that adding new-style code to an old-style module (without refactoring the old functions) is fine.

- PRC-103 (2026-11-12): added rates.quote_with_surcharge. Moved the surcharge % table to
  rates.FUEL_SURCHARGE_PCT (single source); legacy/billing.fuel_surcharge now imports it (same behavior).
  New function raises DomainError E_BAD_ZONE / E_BAD_WEIGHT; it validates BEFORE calling the old
  quote(), which raises ValueError. Existing quote/base_rate were left on ValueError because the frozen
  tests/test_rates.py expects ValueError. Money (parcelo/money.py) handles half-up cent rounding.
  New tests/unit/test_rates_surcharge.py, CHANGELOG bullet. Suite: 24 passed.
  RESULT: CI passed, review REQUESTED CHANGES: (a) returned a float (`(base+surcharge).cents / 100`) and
  should have returned `Money`; (b) depended on parcelo.legacy (the test imported billing, and I edited
  legacy/billing.py to import from rates). The fix: return Money, keep FUEL_SURCHARGE_PCT in rates.py
  as a copy, leave legacy/billing.py untouched, and hardcode the test expectations. Both rules are now in [[ticket-checklist]].
  Validation-before-legacy-call (DomainError first, then call old ValueError function) was NOT criticized.

- PRC-104 (2026-11-12): added customers.deactivate_customer (DomainError E_NOT_FOUND for missing id,
  E_BAD_STATE f"{id} is inactive" if already inactive; sets active=False, audit "customer.deactivated",
  returns customer). Used `db.customers.get(id)` directly (old get_customer raises KeyError).
  Chose E_NOT_FOUND (direct lookup) over E_UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER (shipments uses that one for a *referenced* customer).
  Left old-style add/get_customer (ValueError/KeyError/uuid) untouched; no timestamp field added because the

  New tests/unit/test_customers_deactivate.py (3 tests) + CHANGELOG bullet. Suite: 8 passed.
  RESULT: CI passed + review APPROVED on first try. This is the 2nd first-try approval in a row from following the full checklist.

- PRC-105 (2026-11-12): NEW module parcelo/refunds.py create_refund(invoice_id, amount) + models.Refund

  RESULT: CI passed + review APPROVED on first try (3rd in a row with the full checklist). The extra

- PRC-106 (2026-11-12): added invoices.late_fee_for(invoice_id) -> Money. db.invoices.get -> E_NOT_FOUND;
  days_late = (clock.now() - issued_at).days - 30 (whole days); <=0 -> Money.zero(); else

  New tests/unit/test_invoices_late_fee.py (10 cases) + CHANGELOG bullet. Suite: 14 passed.
  RESULT: CI passed + review APPROVED on first try (4th in a row with the full checklist). Confirms: copying

- PRC-107 (2026-11-12): added shipments.mark_delivered(shipment_id): get_shipment -> E_NOT_FOUND; status in
  ("cancelled","delivered") -> E_BAD_STATE f"{id} is {status}"; sets status + delivered_at=clock.now() (field

  RESULT: CI passed + review APPROVED on first try (5th in a row with the full checklist). Confirms: reusing

- PRC-108 (2026-11-12): added reports.outstanding_by_customer() -> {customer_id: Money}. Invoice -> customer goes

# Parcelo ticket checklist: required for EVERY ticket (code review rejects otherwise)

Go through this before you call any ticket done. CI passing is not enough, because review enforces these rules.
(Track record: tickets that followed every item, PRC-102, PRC-104, PRC-105, PRC-106, PRC-107, PRC-108, PRC-109, PRC-110, PRC-111, PRC-112, PRC-113, PRC-114, PRC-141, PRC-142, PRC-144, PRC-145, PRC-146, PRC-147, PRC-148, PRC-149, PRC-154 (first ticket after ALL 12 items existed), PRC-155 (read-only list query), PRC-156 (pricing + settings.py) PRC-157 (invoices.hold_invoice, idempotent state change; template = item 9) PRC-158 (new returns module with per-shipment cap; template = item 13) PRC-160 (shipments.mark_returned, item 9 + new `[PRC-NNN]` changelog format) PRC-161 (customers.rebate_for, read-only tiered Money calc; template at end of file) PRC-162 (invoices.invoices_by_status, item 11 template) PRC-163 (customers.lock_customer, item 9 bool-flag template) and PRC-164 (vouchers.issue_voucher, item 13 + Money cap, template at end of file) and PRC-165 (reports.shipments_without_invoice, anti-join list query) and PRC-166 (invoices.escalate_invoice, item 9 + settings.py min amount), were approved on the first try. Tickets that missed one, PRC-101, PRC-103, PRC-143 (ids, see item 8), PRC-150 (stored a float money field, see item 4), PRC-151 (no docs/api.md line + list not sorted by id, see items 10-11), PRC-152 (repeat state change raised instead of being an idempotent no-op, see item 9) and PRC-153 (business threshold kept in the module and not in parcelo/settings.py, see item 12) and PRC-159 (CHANGELOG bullet in the old `(PRC-NNN)` suffix format; must now be `- [PRC-NNN] ...`, see item 1), were rejected.)
NOTE: house conventions CHANGE over time (CHANGELOG format changed in PRC-171). Before following a remembered rule, check that the repo's newest examples still agree with it. If they don't, the newest repo evidence wins, so update this file.
NOTE: a ticket saying "X that is already <other state> must fail" does NOT mean "already <target state>" fails. Same-state repeats are always a silent no-op.
NOTE: reviewers keep adding NEW house rules that CI doesn't check. Before coding, look for docs/ (api.md, CONTRIBUTING, etc.)
and READ any docs file that lists public functions or conventions, then follow it.
When a ticket says "the same logic already exists in parcelo/legacy/...": READ it for reference, then reimplement it as new code + constants. Never import or call it (see item 5).
This also applies when the ticket names a specific legacy helper to use (PRC-114: "days_between already has the day arithmetic"). Reimplementing it privately was approved.
"Paid invoices are left out" means only "open" ones count, so use an allowlist `("open",)`, which also leaves out "void" (approved in PRC-114).
If the ticket says "round the same way as <legacy/old float code>", still use Money (half-up cents). That was approved in PRC-110. Point out any half-cent differences in the handoff.
Reports: if the ticket says "every customer", seed every customer with zero. Don't filter by status unless the ticket says to (PRC-147 counted all statuses and was approved). Counts and labels are plain int/str.
Small extra validations beyond the ticket (e.g. non-positive amount, over-limit) were accepted in PRC-105 and are good practice.
They need registered error codes and tests.

   Create the `## Unreleased` section at the top if it is missing.

4. **Money = `Money`, never float.** Any new function that returns or passes a currency amount must
   use `Money` from `parcelo.money`. Wrap old float values with `Money.parse(x)`, and RETURN the
   `Money` object. Do NOT convert back with `.cents / 100` or `float(...)`. Tests compare against Money
   (e.g. `== Money.parse("14.56")`), and you should check the Money API in money.py first. PRC-103 was rejected for returning a float.
   **DEFAULT: when you WRITE a money field, store the Money object** (`entity.field = money`). Any `float(...)` or `/ 100` on
   money in your diff is a red flag to reviewers. PRC-150 was REJECTED for storing Customer.credit_limit back as a float even
   though the function returned Money. Read old float values with `Money.parse(entity.field)`, and tests should assert Money, not floats.
   NARROW EXCEPTION (approved only in PRC-113): store back as float ONLY IF you grep and find existing old code that does
   float arithmetic on that exact field (e.g. Invoice.amount summed by reports.revenue_total / customers.outstanding_balance),
   so that storing Money would break it. If you use it, name those consumers in a code comment AND add a test that calls them.
   No such consumer means store Money. If unsure, store Money and mention it in the handoff.
   APPROVED TEMPLATE for pricing on top of the old float quote() (PRC-156 rates.heavy_quote; same shape as PRC-110):
   ```python
   if zone not in ZONE_BASE: raise DomainError("E_BAD_ZONE", ...)            # validate BEFORE old ValueError code
   if isinstance(w, bool) or not isinstance(w, (int, float, Decimal)): raise DomainError("E_BAD_WEIGHT", ...)
   if w <= 0: raise DomainError("E_BAD_WEIGHT", ...)
   price = Money.parse(quote(w, zone))
   excess = Decimal(str(w)) - Decimal(str(settings.HEAVY_THRESHOLD_KG))      # Decimal(str()) avoids float noise
   if excess > 0: price = price + Money.parse(settings.HEAVY_PER_KG_SURCHARGE).scale(excess)
   return price
   ```
   Test weights must avoid half-cent results: old quote() uses float round() (62.125 -> 62.12).

8. **IDs only via `ids.new_id("<prefix>")`** (format `prefix_000001`; support tooling depends on it). PRC-143 was
   rejected for this even though the main module already called ids.new_id, so be thorough:
   `grep -rn "uuid\|new_id\|_id = f\|id=f" <changed files>` across code AND tests; read parcelo/ids.py; never copy
   id code from old-style modules (invoices.py/customers.py use uuid); in tests assert the exact id
   (`== "pku_000001"`, ids reset per test) or regex `^pku_\d{6}$`, not just `startswith`.
   GOTCHA: the counter is GLOBAL across prefixes. Ids created in the fixture (e.g. shp_000001) shift yours (dsp_000002),
   so count the new_id calls the fixture makes before you hardcode the expected id. customers.add_customer (uuid)
   does NOT consume the counter, but create_shipment does (PRC-149: fixture shipment = shp_000001, children from shp_000002).
   If the diff already complies, say so explicitly in the handoff (file:line of the new_id call).
   If the ticket creates no ids (e.g. PRC-145 upgrade_tier), new_id isn't needed. Calling an old uuid creator
   (add_customer) only through its public API in fixtures was accepted. Don't rewrite it unless asked. (PRC-146 confirmed this: write_off added to invoices.py, issue_invoice's uuid left as-is, approved.)
9. **State transitions must be IDEMPOTENT (PRC-152 REJECTED for this).** Callers retry on timeouts, so if the
   entity is ALREADY IN THE TARGET STATE, return it unchanged: no error, no second event, no timestamp rewrite.
   Check this FIRST (right after lookup), before the allowlist:
   ```python
   s = get_shipment(id)            # E_NOT_FOUND
   if s.status == "lost":          # already in target state -> no-op
       return s
   if s.status not in LOSABLE_STATUSES:   # allowlist of source states
       raise DomainError("E_BAD_STATE", ...)
   ```
   Otherwise use an ALLOWLIST tuple of source states (`("created",)`, `("paid",)`, `("open",)`) -> E_BAD_STATE, not
   a denylist. The target state itself must NOT end up hitting E_BAD_STATE.
   Status-string variant approved in PRC-157 (invoices.hold_invoice): lookup -> `if inv.status == "on_hold": return inv`
   -> allowlist HOLDABLE_STATUSES=("open",) -> set status + `<verb>_at = clock.now()` (new model field, default None)
   -> `events.emit("invoice.held", id, from_status=prev, to_status="on_hold")`.
   Tests: happy path; missing -> E_NOT_FOUND; each bad state the ticket names -> E_BAD_STATE + fields unchanged +
   OUTBOX == []; **"call twice -> second call returns same entity, status unchanged, exactly ONE event in OUTBOX,
   timestamps unchanged"**. Do NOT write a "twice fails" test (older tickets PRC-107/142 did; that rule is now obsolete).
   Applies to any set-state op (cancel, deliver, deactivate, reactivate, void, reopen, mark_*, upgrade_tier...). For
   boolean flags (active=False/True), "already in target value" -> return unchanged too. Say "Idempotent" in the docstring.
   APPROVED TEMPLATE (PRC-154, customers.reactivate_customer):
   ```python
   customer = db.customers.get(customer_id)
   if customer is None: raise DomainError("E_NOT_FOUND", customer_id)
   if customer.active: return customer          # no-op, no event
   customer.active = True
   events.emit("customer.reactivated", customer.id)
   return customer
   ```

   partner team read that file). Add one line per function, in this format:
   ``- `<module>.<func>(<args>)`: <short description>`` e.g. ``- `shipments.mark_lost(shipment_id)`: mark a shipment lost``.
   Read docs/api.md first and put the line next to that module's other entries. Create the file if it's missing. Private
   `_helpers` don't need entries. This applies to new modules too (refunds, claims, pickups...).
11. **Any function returning a LIST of entities must sort by `id` ascending**: `sorted(items, key=lambda x: x.id)`.
   Do NOT rely on dict/storage/creation order (PRC-151 rejected; the support export diffs these lists between runs).
   Docstring should say "sorted by id". Test: insert entities so storage order != id order (e.g. create, then
   reassign/mutate, or insert directly into db out of order) and assert the sorted result. It returns a new list.
   Apply the same idea to report dicts/lists of entities where order is visible.
   APPROVED TEMPLATE (PRC-155, customers.customers_by_tier, filter-by-enum query):
   ```python
   if tier not in TIERS:                       # validate FIRST -> E_BAD_INPUT (case-sensitive; None/"" fail too)
       raise DomainError("E_BAD_INPUT", f"unknown tier {tier!r}")
   return sorted((c for c in db.customers.values() if c.tier == tier), key=lambda c: c.id)
   ```
   Tests: match-only + sorted (re-store `db.customers` items reversed to break storage order), known value with no
   matches -> [], empty store -> [], parametrized bad values -> E_BAD_INPUT + OUTBOX == [], result is a new list.
12. **Business numbers live in `parcelo/settings.py` (PRC-153 REJECTED for this).** Any threshold, limit, cap, rate,
   percentage, fee, day count, or tier table that Finance/the business could change goes in parcelo/settings.py as a
   named UPPER_CASE constant (create the file if it's missing, and read it first so you can reuse existing names).
   Code imports it (`from parcelo import settings` -> `settings.REVIEW_MAX_OPEN_INVOICES`). The function body must have NO bare
   business literals like `3`, `250.00`, `0.015`, or `30`, and module-level constants in the feature module are NOT enough.
   Money thresholds: store a string/Decimal in settings and wrap it with `Money.parse(settings.X)` at use (or Money in settings if
   money.py has no import cycle). This also applies when copying constants out of legacy (item 5): put the copy in
   settings.py, not the feature module. Tests may hardcode expected values, but boundary tests should reference
   `settings.X` (or monkeypatch it) so a Finance change shows up clearly. Status allowlist tuples like ("open",) are NOT business
   numbers and can stay in the module. Grep your diff: `grep -nE "[^a-zA-Z_][0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?" <changed .py>` and check that every hit is
   0/1/an index or comes from settings.

